---
title: "Credits and licences"
subtitle: "The open work Flux is built on, and what to cite when you use it"
---

Flux is free and open source under the MIT licence. It stands on a great deal of work by other
people. This page names the parts you are most likely to meet. The complete list, with every
bundled library and its licence, is in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Colormaps and palettes

The colour collections in the palette and colormap pickers come from these projects. If a
figure's colours matter to your argument, cite the map you used.

| Collection | Made by | Cite or credit | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flexoki | Steph Ango | [stephango.com/flexoki](https://stephango.com/flexoki) | MIT |
| matplotlib | The Matplotlib Development Team | Hunter (2007), *Computing in Science & Engineering* 9, 90–95, [doi:10.1109/MCSE.2007.55](https://doi.org/10.1109/MCSE.2007.55) | Matplotlib licence |
| Crameri | Fabio Crameri | Crameri (2018), Scientific colour maps, Zenodo, [doi:10.5281/zenodo.1243862](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1243862); Crameri, Shephard and Heron (2020), *Nature Communications* 11, 5444, [doi:10.1038/s41467-020-19160-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19160-7) | MIT |
| Paul Tol | Paul Tol | Tol, Colour Schemes, SRON Technical Note SRON/EPS/TN/09-002, [personal.sron.nl/~pault](https://personal.sron.nl/~pault/) | BSD-3-Clause |
| cmasher | Ellert van der Velden | van der Velden (2020), *Journal of Open Source Software* 5(46), 2004, [doi:10.21105/joss.02004](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.02004) | BSD-3-Clause |
| ColorBrewer | Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower and The Pennsylvania State University | Harrower and Brewer (2003), *The Cartographic Journal* 40, 27–37, [doi:10.1179/000870403235002042](https://doi.org/10.1179/000870403235002042) | Apache-2.0 |

Flux's "green" ramp in the Flexoki palette is the author's own, built around Paul Tol's bright
green as its main shade; Flexoki's green is kept under the name "olive". The house maps in the Flexoki collection were made for fluxplot.

Some maps in the matplotlib collection have their own authors: viridis, magma, inferno and
plasma (Nathaniel J. Smith, Stéfan van der Walt and Eric Firing, CC0); cividis (Nuñez, Anderton
and Renslow, 2018, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0199239](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0199239));
turbo (Anton Mikhailov, Google, Apache-2.0); twilight (Bastian Bechtold); coolwarm (Kenneth
Moreland, 2009); cubehelix (D. A. Green, 2011); and the ColorBrewer maps.

The colour-vision simulation in **View as** uses the model of Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes
(2009), *IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics* 15, 1291–1298,
[doi:10.1109/TVCG.2009.113](https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2009.113).

## Fonts and icons

The interface and exported slides use **Gelasio** (The Gelasio Project Authors, SIL Open Font
License 1.1). Mathematics is set with **KaTeX** and its fonts (Khan Academy and contributors,
MIT). Most interface icons come from **Lucide** (ISC).

## Writing, citing and reading

- Spelling and grammar checking uses [Harper](https://writewithharper.com) (Apache-2.0), which
  runs on your machine.
- The built-in Nature, Science and Cell citation styles come from the Citation Style Language
  project through the [Zotero Style Repository](https://www.zotero.org/styles), under CC BY-SA
  3.0. Each style file names its authors, and Flux copies it into your project unchanged.
- References are parsed and formatted with [citation.js](https://citation.js.org) (MIT) and
  citeproc-js.
- Reader displays PDFs with [pdf.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/) (Mozilla, Apache-2.0).
- The editor is [CodeMirror](https://codemirror.net) (MIT).
- Library and Reader look up references and open-access copies through Crossref, OpenAlex,
  Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, PubMed Central, arXiv and bioRxiv.

The journal export presets follow the public author guidelines of Nature, Science, Cell and
bioRxiv. Flux is not affiliated with or endorsed by those journals.

## Figures, 3D and video

- Plots edited in Flux keep matplotlib's behaviour: the colour scales, tick placement and
  layout rules are ported from [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org).
- 3D models are drawn with [three.js](https://threejs.org) (MIT).
- Slide video export runs [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) as a separate program, under the GNU GPL
  version 3. Its licence and notice sit beside the executable in the app.
- Several easing curves follow the rate functions of
  [Manim Community](https://www.manim.community) (MIT).

## The app itself

Flux is built with [Electron](https://www.electronjs.org), [Svelte](https://svelte.dev) and
TypeScript. Word and Quarto export use [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and
[Pandoc](https://pandoc.org), and LaTeX output uses [TinyTeX](https://yihui.org/tinytex/), each
installed only when you ask for it.

## Inspiration

Two apps shaped how Flux works: [Figma](https://www.figma.com/) was the main inspiration for
Figure, and [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/) for Paper. Flux contains no code from either and is
not affiliated with them.
